title: This fund manager tunes out AI hype to flag the infrastructure stocks to buy now. Think roads, water and telecom towers.
excerpt: Lazard portfolio manager Bertrand Cliquet says infrastructure companies are worth more than the AI hype sometimes linked to them.
content_html:
Barbara Kollmeyer

Tue, August 11, 2026 at 8:39 AM CDT 6 min read

Getting investors to look past the dazzle of artificial intelligence and data centers toward ordinary roads, bridges and cell towers is a fairly tall order these days.

That's the strategy at the $12.3 billion Lazard Global Listed Infrastructure Portfolio fund GLIFX, the Irish-domiciled Lazard Global Listed Infrastructure Equity Fund and the newer Lazard Listed Infrastructure ETF GLIX, seeking out opportunities in energy, water, transport and communications.

  • If you can answer this one question, you'll never worry about money again

The funds focus on lower-risk infrastructure businesses, which act as a tidy diversifier between bonds and equities, portfolio manager Bertrand Cliquet told MarketWatch in an interview on Monday.

Infrastructure investments have an important GDP multiplier effect that can foster significant economic growth by keeping basic services available and flowing, Cliquet said. "If you don't grow your infrastructure and your people spend their lives stuck in traffic, you know it's a massive GDP loss."

Cliquet said the funds seek out companies subject to regulatory agreements or concession contracts that offer long-term cash flow, which helps drive predictable patterns of returns and capital preservation for investors in those businesses.

"Historically it was a sector that was very pedestrian from an organic-growth standpoint, and what we've seen is a real transformation in terms of the ability of companies to build stuff," said the portfolio manager.

He said investors need to look beyond megatrends of artificial intelligence and data centers when looking at these stocks — one reason the fund is 26% exposed to the U.S. but more than 50% weighted to Europe and the U.K. via names such as Ferrovial NL:FER and Vinci FR:DG.

"If you listen to earnings calls from most U.S. regulated utilities, they'll mostly be about AI and data centers. In Europe, we find a very compelling range of long-term drivers," he said.

For example, the importance of energy transition has increased since the start of the Ukraine war, while recurrent European droughts are driving companies to "invest very heavily" in water resources and desalination plants. Cliquet said such drivers for companies can stretch beyond five years, while data-center investment is more "icing on the cake."

The U.S. is still an important market for the Lazard funds. A top holding is U.K. electricity and gas utility National Grid UK:NG NGG, which has 45% of its operations in the U.S.

如今，让投资者超越令人眼花缭乱的人工智能和数据中心，转向普通道路、桥梁和手机信号塔是一项相当艰巨的任务。

这就是价值 123 亿美元的 Lazard 全球上市基础设施投资组合基金 GLIFX、爱尔兰注册的 Lazard 全球上市基础设施股票基金和较新的 Lazard 上市基础设施 ETF GLIX 的策略，寻找能源、水、交通和通信领域的机会。

投资组合经理 Bertrand Cliquet 在周一接受 MarketWatch 采访时表示，这些基金专注于风险较低的基础设施业务，这些业务是债券和股票之间的一个良好的多元化投资工具。

克利凯表示，基础设施投资具有重要的 GDP 乘数效应，可以通过保持基本服务的可用和流动来促进显着的经济增长。 “如果你不发展你的基础设施，而你的人民一生都困在交通中，你就知道这是一个巨大的 GDP 损失。”

克利凯表示，这些基金寻找受监管协议或特许合同约束、提供长期现金流的公司，这有助于为这些企业的投资者带来可预测的回报和资本保值模式。

这位投资组合经理表示：“从历史上看，从有机增长的角度来看，这是一个非常乏味的行业，而我们所看到的是公司制造能力方面的真正转变。”

他表示，投资者在关注这些股票时，需要超越人工智能和数据中心的大趋势——这就是该基金 26% 的敞口投资于美国，但超过 50% 的权重投资于欧洲和英国（通过 Ferrovial NL:FER 和 Vinci FR:DG 等名称）的原因之一。

“如果你听过大多数美国受监管公用事业公司的财报电话会议，你会发现它们主要是关于人工智能和数据中心的。 在欧洲，我们发现了一系列非常引人注目的长期驱动因素，”他说。

例如，自乌克兰战争爆发以来，能源转型的重要性日益凸显，而欧洲反复出现的干旱正促使企业“大力投资”水资源和海水淡化厂。 克利奎特表示，这种对公司的驱动力可能会持续五年以上，而数据中心投资则更像是“锦上添花”。

美国仍然是拉扎德基金的重要市场。 其中最大的控股公司是英国电力和天然气公用事业公司英国国家电网：NG NGG，该公司 45% 的业务位于美国。
